source_review.notes: Retrieved and reviewed all ten final destinations: primary MonetDB/X100, Neumann compilation, Kersten comparative, and Leis morsel-driven papers; current DuckDB internals/execution-format documentation; current Apache Arrow columnar specification; current Velox vector and expression documentation; and PostgreSQL 18 JIT documentation. Checked batch/vector rationale, data-centric compilation, controlled paradigm comparison, morsel/NUMA scheduling, push-based chunks, vector encodings, validity and nested layouts, expression/encoding behavior, and scoped JIT acceleration. Research, format, and product claims are separately bounded.

Checked logical cardinality, physical slots, live selection, validity, and output cardinality are not conflated.
Checked w+h/b is explicitly described as dispatch-only and not a latency or complete cost model.

evidence: Reviewed filter correctness as retaining exactly TRUE positions from ordered selection S under SQL three-valued logic.
Reviewed projection alignment over S' and representation-independence conditional on decoding/lifetime correctness.
Reviewed pipeline composition, breaker dependency, morsel state partition, and bounded-backpressure arguments.

evidence: Reviewed empty and partial-tail batches, all-NULL/all-selected/no-selected cases, sparse/dense and repeated/ordered selection policies.
Reviewed invalid payload behind NULL, dictionary and nested bounds, lazy/constant/sequence encoding, compaction, base-buffer retention, aliasing, and mutation.
Reviewed huge/small batches, early limit, compilation/warm-up, pipeline breakers, build publication, morsel loss/duplication, skew/NUMA, backpressure, cancellation, and malformed untrusted arrays.

evidence: Checked equal column cardinality, in-range selection, validity alignment, offsets/indices, buffer lifetime, and exclusive/shared mutation rules.
Checked selected rows are evaluated once under SQL type/NULL/effect contracts and output order/multiplicity remain correct.
Checked breaker state publication, morsel ownership, queue bounds, backpressure, cancellation, error, and early-stop propagation.
invariant_checking.notes: Physical adaptation may alter batching, encoding, placement, and worker ownership but not logical results or governed resource bounds.

evidence: Reviewed batch well-formedness requirements for flat, nullable, dictionary, and nested representations.
Reviewed scalar-equivalence proofs for filter and projection and their composition across a pipeline.
Reviewed atomic morsel transitions and credit-based in-flight bounds under explicit scheduler and cleanup assumptions.
proof_review.notes: No proof assumes SIMD, speedup, lock freedom, arbitrary extension correctness, or failure-transparent distributed execution.

evidence: The finite model explicitly excludes arbitrary SQL behavior, nonflat encodings, ownership, SIMD, compilation, scheduling, spill, errors, and performance.
The amortization expression names omitted cache, latency, memory, branch, and cancellation forces.
Versioned DuckDB, Velox, Arrow, and PostgreSQL observations are not generalized into universal execution-engine properties.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Mathematical invariants, finite execution, primary research experiments, format specifications, and current documentation are labeled by evidence type.

evidence: Repository verification passed one standard-library Python snippet with exact eleven-line stdout, empty stderr, zero exit status, and recorded Python 3.14.4 toolchain.
Independent recomputation reproduced all nine outcomes, three batch selections, projected output, predicate counts, and dispatch-only arithmetic.
All ten source artifacts were retained under artifacts/references/DBE-059 and every repository-local link resolved.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No DuckDB/Velox/PostgreSQL/Arrow runtime, SIMD/compiler, hardware-counter, NUMA, scheduler, fault, spill, backpressure, concurrency, or production experiment was executed.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed progression from logical vector semantics through encodings, NULL/selection behavior, finite batch equivalence, pipeline graphs, push/pull, batch sizing, SIMD, fusion/compilation, current systems, parallel morsels, backpressure, verification, and alternatives. Mechanism, representation, guarantee, scheduling, and policy remain distinct.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed diagnosis with batch cardinalities/fill, selection density, encodings/flattening/compaction, retained bytes, kernel/fusion boundaries, compilation/warm-up/code cache, pipeline dependencies, morsels/steals/NUMA, queues/backpressure, memory/spill, first/total latency, CPU counters, concurrency, cancellation, and error cleanup. pedagogical_review.notes: The chapter begins from logical rows rather than arrays, derives NULL-aware selection, provides an exact batch/scalar oracle, explains pipeline decomposition and scheduling, compares ten alternatives, lists fourteen misconceptions, includes ten distinct examples, and progresses five exercises to a parallel hash-join scheduler with complete answers.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary-source, specification/documentation, mathematical, executable-snippet, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic, DuckDB/Velox/PostgreSQL/Arrow or execution-engine maintainer, compiler/architecture, concurrency, security, performance, reliability, operations, or independent practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and finite model prove neither arbitrary SQL/type/encoding semantics, safe untrusted vector parsing, target-engine correctness, SIMD or compiled-code correctness, lock-free or failure-safe parallel scheduling, workload-independent batch/fusion/compilation superiority, benchmark reproducibility across hardware, certification, nor deployment fitness.
